props.name: zinc oxide–chromic oxide catalyst

props.name: Methanol is produced when carbon oxide–hydrogen mixtures in theoretical proportions or wit

evidence.quote: are passed over suitable catalysts at temperatures of from 300 to 500° C. and 55 at pressures in excess of 50 atmospheres.
If operating 6 conditions are not correctly adjusted, or if — improper catalysts are employed, side-reac- tions occur producing products other than methanol and water.

props.statement: Methanol is produced when carbon oxide–hydrogen mixtures in theoretical proportions or with excess hydrogen pass over suitable catalysts at 300 to 500° C. and above 50 atmospheres; wrong conditions or improper catalysts cause side reactions.

props.name: Optimum results are obtained when hydrogen exceeds the theoretical proportion to carbon ox

the presence of.an‘éxcess of hydrogen over that theoretically required to react with the carbon oxides present tends to prevent the occurrence of undesirable side- reactions which produce free'carbon, meth- ane, water, etc., rather than methanol.

props.statement: Optimum results are obtained when hydrogen exceeds the theoretical proportion to carbon oxides, since excess hydrogen tends to prevent side reactions producing free carbon, methane, water and so on.

props.statement: In a recirculating system fed with make-up gas of non-theoretical proportions the circulating gas composition drifts; with excess hydrogen the carbon monoxide falls until practically no methanol is produced; the same holds for CO2–H2 mixtures.

props.name: circulating system with converter (catalyst bomb) G, heat exchanger D, condenser O, circulating pump R (Fig. 1)
props.description: Make-up gas enters at A and mixes with circulating gas at B; heat exchanger D; converter G with catalyst basket H holding catalyst sections J (pre-catalyst/purifier) and J'; electric heating elements K, K'; condenser O; receiver P; circulating pump R.

evidence.quote: From the exchanger the warmed gas passes downward through pipe F into the converter (catalyst bomb) &.
This gas mixes with the gas of the circulating system at connection B, and the __. mixed gases pass upward into the internal ® | passage C of heat exchanger D.
The ele- vated temperature in the converter (7 is large- ly maintained by the heat of reaction, but -y9 supplementary heat is provided for by means | of electric heating elements K, K’,
In operating the process, the circulating pump K serves to circulate the gas through the system to over- come pressure drops due to friction in the pipes and catalyst chamber.

Section J is designed to act as a “pre-catalyst” or purifier, to destroy or absorb any catalyst ; poisons which may be present in the gas, and thus to preserve the catalytic activity of sec- tion J’ for the methanol reaction.
